resources.string: Wireless debugging is ON.\n\nadbd is listening on a random port, and it announces that port over mDNS. Find it from the host with host-connect.sh, which reads `adb mdns services` and then validates each entry.
Wireless debugging is OFF.\n\nThe host cannot reach this device over adb.
Wireless debugging state is unknown (setting never written on this device).
Periodic check: ON. Re-enables wireless debugging if something switches it off. Doze can stretch the interval well past 15 minutes on an unplugged device.
Periodic check: NOT REGISTERED. Reopen this app to schedule it.
Write refused: no WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS.\n\nRun: adb shell pm grant ai.liquid.pipette.adbconnector android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Accepts the system\'s "Allow wireless debugging on this network?" dialog, so this device stays reachable over adb after it moves between access points. When the lab sets pipette_keep_screen_on, it also turns the screen back on while plugged in. Only receives events from the system UI.
Dialog accepter: ON. Approves new access points by itself, so a roam no longer switches wireless debugging off.
Dialog accepter: registered but NOT RUNNING. The system has not bound it; enable it once in Settings > Accessibility > Installed apps. The wifi rejoin monitor and the screen keeper are off with it.
Dialog accepter: NOT REGISTERED. This device will lose wireless debugging when it moves to an access point it has not approved before.
Screen keeper: ON. Turns the screen back on while plugged in. Set global pipette_keep_screen_on to 0 to let it sleep.
Screen keeper: off (global pipette_keep_screen_on is not 1, or the dialog accepter is not running).
Write failed: %1$s. See logcat tag pipette-adb-connector.
